title: Circuit size yields polynomial-time advice
statement: Let $L$ be a language of finite binary words, and let $a,k\in\mathbb N$. If $L$ has a family of Boolean circuits with fan-in at most two whose circuit on inputs of length $n$ has size at most $a(n+1)^k$, then there is a natural number $c$ such that $L$ is decidable by a finite Turing machine with advice of length $(12a^2+1)(n+1)^{2k}$ and running time at most a constant multiple of $n^c+1$ on inputs of length $n$.
hypotheses_covered: L is a language of binary words
L has fan-in-two circuit size at most a(n+1)^k at every input length
